name: permission-denied
description: An account whose group is missing the rest-api or read policy. RouterOS answers this with HTTP 500 and 'not enough permissions', NOT 403 - branching on the status code would classify a permissions problem as a server fault and tell the operator to look in the wrong place. This scenario proves the message names the exact /user group add command that fixes it, and that the run ends cleanly rather than half-importing. The router menu is refused too, so no assets are produced and the summary explains the version, service, and policy preconditions in one line. request_count pins the fail-fast: the permission 500 is excluded from get_json's transient retry list, so the first refused menu costs exactly one request instead of four backoff attempts.  The task now ENDS IN ERROR rather than reporting a successful run with zero assets: a refused credential and an empty tenant are otherwise the same result, and only the exit status separates them.

log_contains: the account's group is missing a policy
